title: One hour. One record.
text: We built ProofGrid to turn solar reports into evidence reviewers can trace and test. The working application registered a published historical solar reference: twenty four hours totaling forty point seven one nine kilowatt hours. It then rejected all twenty four repeated meter hours, even after the readings changed. For the Renewable Energy and Energy Trading track, we connected data quality, atomic registration, and verifiable exports in one workflow for small solar operators and community energy reviewers.

title: One workspace. Clear decisions.
text: We brought the energy profile, candidate total, raw readings, and quality findings into a single review workspace. The input format uses a meter identifier, a supplied capacity bound, and hourly energy values in a simple CSV. Each timestamp identifies one UTC hour. Reviewers can connect a chart peak to its underlying reading and check the relevant finding in the same interface. Synthetic examples and published historical data demonstrate this consistent review process.

title: Three faults. Clear corrections.
text: We implemented explainable checks that turn data problems into specific findings. The faulty synthetic sample produces three blocking issues, and the batch cannot proceed to registration. Capacity, repeated timestamps, continuity, formatting, and nonnegative energy checks establish a clear input contract. A separate peak comparison flags values for reviewer attention. This distinction keeps blocking rules explicit while supporting informed human judgement on readings that deserve a closer look.

title: Traceable source data
text: We transformed published Open Power System Data and CoSSMic cumulative readings into a traceable hourly solar reference. Its twenty four nominal intervals total forty point seven one nine kilowatt hours, with a peak of seven point nine eight one kilowatt hours. The repository preserves the selected counters, transformation code, attribution, and file hashes. The interface links the resulting readings to their published source and configured ten kilowatt review setting. Regeneration produced identical data hashes.

title: Reviewed. Registered.
text: We connected the review decision to an actual Solidity transaction on a local Ethereum Virtual Machine. The contract records the evidence digest and reserves the meter hour slots in one atomic operation. The demonstrated batch receives a successful block two receipt. Source classification, readings, and verification specifications are committed together, linking the reviewed content to its transaction. This creates an inspectable registration record that reviewers can export and check again.

title: 24 repeated hours blocked
text: We validated duplicate protection by changing the supplied readings and submitting the same twenty four meter hours again. All twenty four occupied slots were detected, and registration was blocked. The changed file could not register those hours a second time in this registry. At the contract level, an automated test submits an overlapping transaction, confirms a reverted receipt, and verifies that no partial registration remains. The enforcement holds across both the interface and contract execution.

title: Four checks. Verifiable evidence.
text: We delivered a portable JSON evidence package and verified the original against four checks. After one reading was altered, the content check identified the mismatch. Verification combines a recomputed digest, registry identity, on-chain registration, and the successful receipt event. The interface makes each result visible, connecting the exported content to its registration evidence. A separate command-line verifier reproduces the content-integrity check outside the application.

title: Built. Tested. Reproducible.
text: ProofGrid delivers an implemented, tested path from solar readings to registered and verifiable evidence. Eleven automated tests pass across validation, contract execution, source classification, and evidence integrity. The demonstrated workflow records twenty four meter hours, blocks repeated registration, and detects an edited export. Four verification checks make the result inspectable. Published code, traceable source data, and documented commands make these results reproducible. Review completed. Evidence registered. Verification delivered. One hour. One record.
